_instructions: Setting descriptors for the configuration composer (see config/configuration/settings-catalog.json). Current values are always read live; descriptors hold no defaults.

settings.description: Whether anyone can sign up (open) or new accounts need an administrator (restricted).
examples: stop new signups
let anyone register
close registration

settings.description: Failed sign-ins on one account, within the window, before sign-in is slowed down.
examples: slow down logins after 3 wrong passwords
allow 10 failed attempts

settings.description: How long, in seconds, a network address is first blocked after too many failed sign-ins.
examples: block an IP for 5 minutes after failed logins
shorter lockout for addresses

settings.description: Most chat sessions one account at this account level may keep.
examples: let base users have 20 chats
anonymous visitors get only 2 sessions

settings.description: Most runs one person may have going at once on one agent owned by an account at this level (a level's own runs at once is capped by it). A person's own level does not limit their runs on other owners' agents.
examples: base users can run 3 tasks at once
one run at a time for anonymous

settings.description: Most people (members and signed-out visitors with a message in the last 30 days) one agent owned by an account at this level may serve; new people are refused beyond it. Absent means no limit.
examples: free owners' agents serve up to 20 people
let plus agents have 500 users
how many users can one agent have
settings.notes: Owners may set a lower number per agent. The administrator level has none.

settings.description: Most people with a run going at the same time on one agent owned by an account at this level; a new person waits outside it. Absent means no limit.
examples: three people at once on a free agent
plus agents serve 25 people at the same time
how many users can chat at once
settings.notes: Owners may set a lower number per agent. The administrator level has none.

settings.description: Whether agents owned by an account at this level may let signed-out visitors chat without a widget.
examples: free agents cannot have anonymous visitors
let plus owners open their agents to the public
public links for free users
settings.notes: Absent means allowed. Widgets are not affected.

settings.description: Most runs going at once on all the agents owned by an account at this level together (people other than administrators); a new message beyond it is refused. Absent means no limit.
examples: free owners get two runs at once
plus owners run 9 things at the same time
how many runs can my agents have going
settings.notes: Must not exceed the loop's scheduler.max_active_runs (the server-wide limit); a policy that does is refused. The administrator level has none.

settings.description: Command processor seconds per day (UTC) on all the agents owned by an account at this level together; past it further commands are refused until midnight UTC. Absent means no limit.
examples: free owners get 15 minutes of compute a day
five hours of commands for plus
daily compute time for agent owners
settings.notes: Counted from the command budget ledger; administrators' own commands are not counted. The administrator level has none.

settings.description: Most automations (scheduled tasks and event triggers) one account may keep alive on agents owned by an account at this level. Absent means the automation ability's own setting decides.
examples: free owners may keep 3 automations
plus allows 50 scheduled tasks
limit background jobs per plan
settings.notes: Caps the automation ability's max_automations_per_user. The administrator level has none.

settings.description: Display name of an account level.
examples: rename the Base level to Member
call anonymous users Guests

settings.description: Total storage, in megabytes, one account at this account level may use across chats, attachments and browser data; empty means unlimited.
examples: give base users 500 MB of storage
anonymous visitors get 10 megabytes
raise my storage limit
let people keep more files
settings.notes: null means unlimited; the composer sets numbers only, so set unlimited in the JSON file.

settings.description: Folder size, in megabytes, of each agent an account at this account level publishes; empty means unlimited.
examples: agent folders can hold 1 GB
limit published agent files to 256 MB
make agents' file space unlimited for operators
settings.notes: null means unlimited; the composer sets numbers only, so set unlimited in the JSON file.

settings.description: How many agents an account at this account level may publish; empty means unlimited.
examples: base users can publish 10 agents
no published agents for anonymous visitors
let people create more agents
settings.notes: null means unlimited; the composer sets numbers only, so set unlimited in the JSON file.

settings.description: Share of the storage limit, in percent, at which users are warned they are running out of space.
examples: warn at 90 percent full
tell me earlier when storage is nearly full
storage warning threshold

settings.description: Share of the storage limit, in percent, for the second, more urgent storage warning. At 100 percent the user's saved automatic cleanup runs and new runs wait for space.
examples: second storage warning at 95 percent
urgent storage warning threshold
warn again when storage is almost full

settings.description: Days a chat can sit unused before its saved history is packed tighter (slower to save, as fast to read).
examples: compress idle chats after 3 days
pack old chats tighter
when are unused chats compressed more

settings.description: Compression level, 1 to 19, for chats unused longer than the idle days: higher saves more space and costs more processing time once; reading is as fast.
examples: compress idle chats harder
lower the idle compression level
idle chat compression strength

settings.description: Days a chat can sit unused before its stored tool results are shortened to what each tool keeps long term (lookups dropped, logs cut to their end). Chats that compacted are shortened behind the compaction point straight away.
examples: trim old tool results after 3 days
keep tool output longer in idle chats
when are old tool results shortened

settings.description: Most characters of each user request copied into an action ledger record, so a recorded critical action still shows what was asked after its chat is deleted. Longer requests are cut and marked as cut.
examples: keep more of the request in the action ledger
shorter request text in recorded actions
how much of my message does the ledger keep

settings.description: Whether saved chat text and files are compressed to save space.
examples: turn off compression
compress saved data
stop squeezing stored text

settings.description: How hard saved data is compressed, from 1 (fastest) to 19 (smallest).
examples: compress harder
faster compression
use maximum compression

settings.description: Smallest item, in bytes, worth compressing; smaller items are stored as they are.
examples: only compress items over 1 KB
skip compressing tiny messages
compress everything regardless of size

settings.description: Model turns one account at this account level may use per day (UTC). Absent means no limit; administrators are never limited. Over it new messages are refused and running work pauses until the next day.
examples: free users get 300 model turns a day
limit anonymous visitors to 60 turns daily
settings.notes: The administrator level has no daily limit; a level without the field has none either.

settings.description: Loop run slots kept for administrators: ordinary runs start only while fewer than the loop's maximum concurrent runs minus this number are going.
examples: keep two run slots for administrators
no reserved slots

settings.description: Run slots kept for agents whose owner is on a paid level (Plus): runs on other owners' agents may hold at most the ordinary slots less this many. 0 keeps nothing back.
examples: keep two run slots for plus users
reserve capacity for paying owners
free users can't take every slot
settings.notes: Runs already going are never stopped; a waiting Free run past free_max_wait_seconds is no longer held back.

settings.description: Seconds a waiting run on a Free owner's agent waits before it is served like a paid one, so Free is slowed but never starved.
examples: free runs wait at most two minutes
stop starving free users
longest wait for free runs

settings.description: Active runs (queued, running or waiting for approval) non-administrators may have on one agent at once. Null means half the loop's maximum concurrent runs, at least 2.
examples: a public agent may run 3 visitors at once
raise the per-agent run cap to 8

settings.description: Model turns non-administrators together may use on one agent per day (UTC). Null means no limit.
examples: each agent serves at most 2000 turns a day
no daily turn cap per agent

settings.description: Processor seconds all shell and python commands of one run (workspace and Sandbox) may use together; past it the run's further commands are refused. Administrators are not limited.
examples: one run may use an hour of command CPU
cap command processor time per run at 10 minutes

settings.description: Processor seconds one account's commands may use per day (UTC). Administrators are not limited.
examples: four hours of command CPU per user per day

settings.description: Commands one run may have going at once.
examples: one command at a time per run

settings.description: Commands one account's runs may have going at once.
examples: each user may run 4 commands at once

excluded./login_protection/account/*: Other login-protection timings; not offered in v1.
excluded./login_protection/address/*: Other login-protection timings; not offered in v1.
excluded./request_limits/**: Request rate limits; tuned in policy.json, not offered in v1.
excluded./pages/**: Which account levels may open each app page; a security setting changed only on its access page or by a reviewed source edit.
excluded./tier_order: Account level order; changed with the account levels themselves.
excluded./tiers/*/allowed_models/**: Ability, tool and model grants act as ceilings (Q8); handled in a later step.
excluded./tiers/*/model_policy/**: Ability, tool and model grants act as ceilings (Q8); handled in a later step.
excluded./storage/compression/algorithm: Only zstd is supported; not a choice.
excluded./storage/compression/skip_media_types/**: List of already-compressed media types; technical, edited in its JSON file.
